key_insight: System 1 models made fast, probability-scored decisions but performed best on medical knowledge and text understanding, with weaker results on clinical judgement and volumetric imaging.
clinical_relevance: These models may warrant further evaluation for narrowly defined clinical tasks, but speed and confidence scores do not establish safe autonomous use.
method: Evaluated four models zero-shot on 86 public tasks across 14 clinical domains and 20 languages.
Grouped tasks into six capability tiers and used AUROC as the primary outcome.
Assessed calibration, language effects, speed and comparisons with published results and generative models.
evidence_signal: Across 179,111 cases, mean AUROC for the best model per task ranged from 0.94 for medical knowledge to 0.69 for volumetric findings; imaging scored 0.09 below text tasks.
watch_item: Performance varied substantially by task and language: triage nurses outperformed the best model, and accuracy on identical questions fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba.
paper_title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
